tagline: Between the two Pioneer ranges, over a 7,800-foot divide.
intro: From Wise River on the Big Hole, the paved Wise River Road runs south the length of the Pioneer Mountains and splits them in two. To the east stand the East Pioneers, rugged glaciated granite peaks over 10,000 feet. To the west the West Pioneers roll away gentler and forested. The road climbs easily between them, through meadows, lodgepole pine and broad willow bottoms, to a 7,800-foot divide between the Wise River, flowing north, and Grasshopper Creek, flowing south.

Somewhere in the West Pioneers stands a lodgepole pine grove over 500 years old, reputed to be the oldest known anywhere. Just off the road the national forest keeps a patch called Crystal Park where anyone may dig for quartz crystals.

moments.title: Coolidge
moments.text: A ghost town keeps company with the abandoned Elkhorn silver mine, which started work in 1872.

moments.title: Elkhorn Hot Springs
moments.text: The hot pools here come naturally heated to around 100 degrees, a soak the state's tourism office suggests after a day on the trails.

practical: Between the Pettengill parking lot and Elkhorn Hot Springs the road is closed from December 1 to May 15, when it serves as a National Recreation Snowmobile Trail.
